senses.gloss: to gaze, be astonished; to be confounded, be waste.
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 2">Gen. R. s. 2</cite>, beg., v. <cite ref="B00162"><he>בָּהָא</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 2">Ib.</cite>, end <he>כבר … יושב ותוֹהֵא</he> once R. S. b. Z. sat gazing (deep in thought, absent-minded).

<cite ref="Taanit 6b:14">Taan. 6ᵇ</cite> (play on <he>ת̇מ̇ט̇ר̇</he>, <cite ref="Amos 4:7">Am. IV, 7</cite>) <he>ת̇הא מקום מ̇ט̇ר̇</he> the place where the rain fell became waste (through destructive showers); a. e.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 3:4:5">Y. Taan. III, 66ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>שלשה … ות׳ שבראן</he> three things God created, and regretted that he had created them. Ib. I, 65ᵇ bot. (ref. to <cite ref="Numbers 23:19">Num. XXIII, 19</cite>) <he>אם יאמר לך אדם … בן אדם אני סופו לִתְהוֹת בו וכ׳</he> if a man says to thee, I am a God, he lies; (if he says,) I am the son of man, he shall regret it; (and if he says,) I will rise to heaven, he says, but he shall not fulfill it.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Nedarim 1:1:14">Y. Ned. I, 36ᵈ</cite> bot. [read:] <he>מכיון שנודר … סופו לתהות מכיון שהוא תוהא וכ׳</he> when one vows in rashness, he will finally regret it, and when he does regret, his sacrifices are like slaughtering profane beasts in the Temple court.
<cite ref="Kiddushin 40b:4">Kidd. 40ᵇ</cite> <he>בתוהא על הראשונות</he> when he is sorry for his good deeds in the past; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Peah 1:1:49">Y. Peah I, 16ᵇ</cite> top.
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 10:10">Num. R. s. 10</cite>, beg. <he>בתוהא על הראשונות</he> (not <he>הרשע</he>; ed. Wil. <he>בתוֹהֶה</he>) when he (the wicked) regrets his doings in the past.
<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 20:16">Ex. R. s. 20<sup>2</sup></cite> <he>התחיל המוכר תוהא</he> the seller was sorry; a. fr.
